vos.title: US Treasury Sanctions Iran's BitBank Over 'Hormuz Safe' Bitcoin Pipeline to IRGC
vos.subTitle:
US Treasury Sanctions Iran's BitBank Over 'Hormuz Safe' Bitcoin Pipeline to IRGC
OFAC designates BitBank, its developer Pishtaz Simorgh Electronic Trade Company, and three associates of financier Babak Zanjani — alleging hundreds of millions in Bitcoin funneled to the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps through a maritime insurance scheme at the Strait of Hormuz.

Cold Open
The US Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control just drew a hard line between maritime chokepoint economics and on-chain settlement rails — and it runs straight through Bitcoin.
On Thursday, Washington sanctioned Iranian crypto exchange BitBank, accusing it of processing Bitcoin payments collected from ships transiting the Strait of Hormuz and routing them to the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps. Treasury alleges the mechanism sits inside a broader architecture used by Iranian financier Babak Zanjani to move hundreds of millions of dollars in Bitcoin to the IRGC.

This is not a routine exchange blacklisting. It is the first time OFAC has explicitly tied a state-backed maritime insurance scheme to a crypto settlement layer — and it reframes how compliance desks, exchanges, and institutional allocators must think about chain-level exposure to sanctioned sovereign actors.

Chronological Timeline & Verified Data
The Designation — Thursday, September 17, 2026
The US Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control announced sanctions against BitBank, an Iranian digital asset exchange. The core allegation: BitBank processed Bitcoin payments received through Iran's Strait of Hormuz maritime scheme, known as Hormuz Safe.
Per Treasury, as of June, the Hormuz Safe Marine Services Authority used BitBank to transfer payments it received onward to the IRGC. Treasury characterized this as part of the architecture used by Babak Zanjani — an Iranian financier — to move hundreds of millions of dollars in Bitcoin to the IRGC.
The Scheme Mechanics
Treasury has previously alleged that Hormuz Safe is part of an IRGC-backed scheme forcing vessels to buy maritime insurance for passage through the Strait of Hormuz — including coverage against seizures by Iran itself. In other words: a protection racket denominated in maritime risk, settled in Bitcoin.
The Strait of Hormuz remains the single most consequential oil transit chokepoint on earth. Any mechanism that monetizes passage through it — and settles that monetization in a censorship-resistant asset — represents a direct collision between sovereign enforcement and permissionless rails.
The Full Designation Package
OFAC's action did not stop at the exchange. The designations include:
BitBank — the Iranian crypto exchangePishtaz Simorgh Electronic Trade Company — BitBank's developerThree associates of Babak Zanjani
This is a multi-entity, multi-layer designation — targeting not just the front-end exchange but the development entity behind it and the human network facilitating flows. That structure signals Treasury is mapping the full operational stack, not just the visible on-ramp.
The Official Statement
US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent framed the action in unambiguous terms:
"Today's designations of Iranian digital asset infrastructure make perfectly clear that efforts to finance the Iranian regime using cryptocurrencies are not beyond OFAC's reach."
The designation is the latest Treasury action aimed at isolating Iran from the international financial system, including through sanctions on digital asset exchanges. The pattern is now well-established: OFAC has repeatedly demonstrated willingness to target crypto infrastructure where it intersects with sanctioned sovereign finance.
Broader Market Context — Same Window
The sanctions headline landed into a market already positioning around macro. Bitcoin traded around 76,938 in the reporting window, up roughly 0.94%, as markets braced for the Federal Reserve's next move. The tape showed a bounce rather than a risk-off reaction — a notable signal that the sanctions news was absorbed as a compliance and geopolitical story, not a systemic liquidity event.
Cross-asset prints from the same window:
ETH ~2,462.61 (+1.62%)SOL ~102.62 (+3.54%)BNB ~750.27 (+3.67%)XRP ~1.30 (+0.67%)ADA ~0.2165 (+11.01%)LINK ~11.55 (+4.08%)XMR ~518.75 (+3.53%)ZEC ~1,486.80 (+8.19%)HYPE ~86.42 (+9.30%)DOGE ~0.08276 (+2.49%)TRX ~0.3358 (+0.06%)XLM ~0.1850 (+1.11%)
The read-through: privacy-adjacent assets (XMR, ZEC) and high-beta altcoins outperformed while Bitcoin consolidated. That divergence matters — it suggests the market is pricing sanctions risk as a narrative catalyst for privacy and non-KYC rails, not as a broad de-risking trigger.

Why This Designation Is Structurally Different
Most exchange sanctions stories follow a familiar template: a mid-tier venue gets blacklisted, its banking rails get severed, and the market shrugs. This one is different on three axes.
First: the settlement asset is Bitcoin, not a stablecoin.
Treasury's allegation centers on Bitcoin transfers — not dollar-pegged tokens, not bank wires. That distinction is critical. Stablecoin flows are inherently traceable through issuer-level freeze capabilities. Bitcoin is not. The allegation that hundreds of millions of dollars moved through this channel implies a sustained, high-volume operation that evaded traditional financial surveillance entirely. That is precisely the scenario Bitcoin's design anticipates — and precisely the scenario OFAC is now publicly documenting.
Second: the underlying activity is maritime coercion, not narcotics or terror financing in the abstract.
The Hormuz Safe scheme, as described by Treasury, forces vessels to purchase insurance for passage through the Strait of Hormuz — including coverage against seizures by Iran itself. This is a protection racket at a global chokepoint, and it is being settled in crypto. That framing gives OFAC a far more potent narrative: crypto is not just a sanctions-evasion tool, it is the payment rail for coercive control of global energy logistics.
Third: the designation targets the developer, not just the exchange.
Including Pishtaz Simorgh Electronic Trade Company — BitBank's developer — in the designation package is a meaningful escalation. It signals that OFAC is willing to pursue the technical builders of sanctioned crypto infrastructure, not merely the operators. For any team building exchange or payment infrastructure with ambiguous jurisdictional exposure, this is a precedent worth studying closely.

The Zanjani Connection
Babak Zanjani is not a peripheral figure in this story. Treasury explicitly names him as the financier whose architecture moved hundreds of millions of dollars in Bitcoin to the IRGC, and the designation package includes three of his associates.
Zanjani's historical profile — a financier previously associated with large-scale sanctions circumvention — makes his alleged pivot into Bitcoin rails a case study in how sanctioned capital adapts. The pattern is consistent: when traditional banking channels close, capital migrates to the rails that remain open. Bitcoin, by design, does not have an issuer who can freeze balances at the protocol level.
The inclusion of three associates suggests Treasury is not treating this as a single-actor problem. It is mapping a network — and network designations tend to precede further network designations.

Trading Angle
What this means for market structure:
The immediate tape reaction was benign — Bitcoin held near 76,938, up modestly, with the market's attention squarely on the Fed. That is the correct read for the spot market: this is a compliance and geopolitical headline, not a liquidity shock. There is no evidence in the verified data of exchange insolvency, customer fund impairment, or contagion to major venues.
But the second-order effects are where the trade lives.
1. Privacy and non-KYC assets are the narrative beneficiaries.
The outperformance in the same window is striking: ZEC +8.19%, XMR +3.53%, HYPE +9.30%, ADA +11.01%. When OFAC publicly documents a hundreds-of-millions Bitcoin sanctions-evasion channel, the market's reflexive conclusion is that privacy demand is structural, not cyclical. Traders should watch whether ZEC and XMR sustain relative strength against Bitcoin in the sessions following the designation — sustained outperformance would confirm the market is pricing a regulatory-driven privacy premium.
2. Compliance risk premium on exchange tokens and CEX-adjacent names.
Any venue with ambiguous jurisdictional exposure now faces a higher perceived tail risk. BNB at 750.27 (+3.67%) and TRX at 0.3358 (+0.06%) are the names to monitor for divergence — TRX's flat print against a broadly green tape is worth noting, though the verified data does not attribute it to this story. The broader point: exchange-adjacent tokens carry a headline-risk beta that spot Bitcoin does not.
3. Bitcoin's "sanctions-resistant" narrative gets tested.
There are two ways the market can read this. Bullish read: OFAC just confirmed, in an official document, that Bitcoin is being used at scale to move value outside the dollar system — a validation of its monetary properties. Bearish read: sustained OFAC focus on Bitcoin rails invites more aggressive chain-analytics enforcement, potential miner-level scrutiny, and increased compliance friction at regulated on-ramps.
The tape's answer so far: mildly bullish, with Bitcoin bouncing into the Fed. But this is a slow-burn story, not a one-day event.
Key levels and monitoring priorities:
Bitcoin: The 76,938 area is the reference print. Watch whether the sanctions headline produces any funding rate dislocation in perpetuals — a spike in funding without a spot move would signal leveraged speculation on the narrative rather than genuine flow.Privacy assets: ZEC near 1,486.80 and XMR near 518.75 are the cleanest expressions of the privacy-premium thesis. Watch open interest on these pairs — rising OI with rising price confirms conviction; rising OI with flat price signals crowded positioning.Exchange tokens: BNB at 750.27 and TRX at 0.3358 as compliance-beta proxies.Macro overlay: The Fed decision dominates near-term direction. The sanctions story is a background variable that could amplify risk-off if it escalates into secondary designations of non-Iranian counterparties.
What would change the thesis:
If OFAC follows this designation with actions against non-Iranian exchanges or payment processors alleged to have facilitated flows, the story shifts from geopolitical isolation to systemic compliance risk — and that would be a genuine market-structure event. Until then, treat this as a narrative catalyst with asymmetric upside for privacy assets and asymmetric headline risk for exchange-adjacent names.
Positioning summary:
Constructive on privacy-adjacent assets on relative-strength confirmationNeutral-to-cautious on exchange tokens into further OFAC headlinesNeutral on Bitcoin spot, with the Fed as the dominant near-term driverWatch for secondary designations as the key escalation signal

vos.title: Project Spotlight: Lighter
vos.subTitle:
Imagine trying to play competitive table tennis, but every time you hit the ball, you have to wait twelve seconds for a referee in another country to mail you a confirmation letter that it landed on the table. That is exactly what trading high-frequency derivatives on a standard blockchain feels like. Market makers and institutional funds cannot operate in an environment where they have to wait for global network consensus just to update a simple limit order. For years, the industry accepted this unbearable latency as the mandatory cost of doing business in decentralized finance.
Lighter protocol dismantles this limitation entirely. It is a high-performance, application-specific zero-knowledge rollup built directly on top of Ethereum. Instead of relying on automated formulas, Lighter operates a fully on-chain central limit order book dedicated exclusively to perpetual futures. It bridges the massive gap between the blistering speed of traditional finance and the cryptographic security of decentralized networks.

This infrastructure matters right now because institutional capital requires absolute verifiable security and zero slippage. Legacy automated market makers simply cannot provide this level of precision. By processing over 100,000 orders per second with less than five milliseconds of latency, Lighter matches the performance of Wall Street infrastructure while never taking custody of user funds. With $39 billion in recent 30-day trading volume and over $1.6 trillion cumulatively, Lighter proves that traders no longer have to compromise between raw speed and sovereign self-custody.
▨ The Problem: What’s Broken?

🔹 The Automated Market Maker Trap → Automated market makers were a brilliant bootstrap mechanism, but they force active traders to endure severe slippage and front-running. A mathematical curve simply cannot react to sudden market volatility as sharply as a dedicated order book. This mechanical lag leaves liquidity providers highly exposed to impermanent loss and leaves traders stuck with terrible execution prices during market panics.
🔹 Crippling Blockchain Latency → Generalized blockchains process every single action sequentially. Whether a user is buying a digital collectible or executing a complex algorithmic hedge, they wait in the exact same line. This concurrency bottleneck introduces massive latency and exorbitant per-order gas fees. This sluggish environment effectively prices high-frequency algorithmic traders entirely out of the decentralized ecosystem.
🔹 The Trust Deficit in App-Chains → To escape latency, several decentralized exchanges moved their matching engines to proprietary application chains secured by independent validator networks. This architectural choice trades mathematical security for economic security. Traders are forced to trust that a small, centralized group of node operators will not collude to reorder trades or manipulate liquidations to their own advantage.
🔹 Extractive Fee Structures → The current decentralized derivatives market relies heavily on a parasitic fee model. Retail users are heavily taxed on both sides of a trade to subsidize the liquidity providers and the protocol treasury. This constant financial extraction stifles organic volume and prevents decentralized venues from genuinely competing with massive centralized exchanges.
▨ What Lighter Is Doing Differently

Lighter refuses to compromise between execution speed and cryptographic security. Instead of forcing a matching engine onto a generalized blockchain, the development team built a hybrid architecture. They deployed a high-performance matching engine written in Golang that runs entirely off the main chain. This sequencer processes orders in a deterministic, single-threaded loop. This is the exact same architectural design that powers the fastest centralized exchanges in the world. By keeping the heavy computational work isolated, the platform easily scales past 100,000 transactions per second.
The critical difference is how Lighter anchors this speed to the blockchain. In traditional off-chain setups, users must trust the operator blindly. Lighter eliminates this trust requirement entirely by utilizing custom Plonky2 zero-knowledge circuits. After the off-chain sequencer matches a batch of trades, a specialized prover network generates a cryptographic receipt. This zero-knowledge proof mathematically guarantees that every single match, margin check, and liquidation adhered strictly to the immutable rules of the exchange.

The protocol then submits this proof to the settlement smart contracts deployed on the Ethereum base layer. These contracts do not calculate the trades. They simply verify the cryptographic math and update the user balances. Because the protocol encodes its entire risk engine directly into these mathematical constraints, the sequencer cannot forge a signature, skip an order in the queue, or execute an unfair liquidation. If an account is healthy, the underlying math prevents it from being liquidated. Lighter delivers the lightning-fast execution of a centralized server while maintaining the absolute, trustless security of the Ethereum network.
▨ Key Components & Features

1️⃣ Off-Chain Sequencer : This is the execution heart of the protocol. It maintains the order book state in local memory and matches buy and sell intents in under five milliseconds. This speed guarantees that market orders fill in a single atomic transaction without the risk of partial execution between block confirmations.
2️⃣ Zero-Knowledge Prover Network :  This component acts as the ultimate cryptographic referee. It takes the matched trades from the sequencer and generates a succinct execution proof demonstrating that price-time priority was perfectly respected. This mechanism completely neutralizes maximal extractable value and front-running risks.
3️⃣ Algorithmic Execution Suite : Lighter natively supports advanced trading tools like Time-Weighted Average Price, Random Slice, and Pegged orders. These allow institutional block traders to dissect massive positions over time to obfuscate their footprint and minimize market impact without requiring complex external software.
4️⃣ Escape Hatch Settlement Layer :  User funds are strictly held in heavily audited Layer 1 smart contracts, never by the Lighter team. If the off-chain sequencer ever goes offline or attempts to censor activity, users can interact directly with the base layer contract to instantly withdraw their capital.
5️⃣ ZK-Enforced Risk Engine : The protocol embeds its margin requirements directly into the zero-knowledge circuits. The system automatically rejects limit orders that deviate too far from the oracle mark price through fat finger prevention and ensures that no trade can inadvertently push a healthy account into an underwater state.
▨ How Lighter Works

🔹 Step 1: A trader deposits their stablecoin collateral directly into the Lighter smart contract deployed on the Ethereum mainnet. This officially locks their funds in a secure, non-custodial vault.
🔹 Step 2: The trader submits a cryptographically signed order intent via the Lighter API or frontend interface, specifying their exact price and size requirements.
🔹 Step 3: The off-chain sequencer receives this intent, places it into a strict first-in-first-out queue, and instantly matches it against resting liquidity in the central limit order book. This provides the trader with millisecond-scale soft finality.
🔹 Step 4: The prover network aggregates a massive batch of these matched trades and computes a zero-knowledge proof. This proof mathematically validates that the sequencer executed the trades perfectly according to the protocol rules.
🔹 Step 5: The protocol submits this cryptographic proof to the Ethereum mainnet settlement contract. The contract verifies the math, permanently updates the official user balances, and finalizes the trading round without requiring expensive on-chain computation.
▨ Value Accrual & Growth Model
✅ Zero-Fee Retail Integration → Lighter solves the retail adoption bottleneck through its Robin Hood strategy. By offering zero maker and zero taker fees for all standard retail accounts, the protocol removes all financial friction from the trading experience. This drives massive organic volume and accelerates user onboarding.
✅ Premium Tier Incentives → Institutional entities, quantitative funds, and market makers pay customized fees to access prioritized API endpoints, higher rate limits, and guaranteed connection stability. This creates a sustainable revenue stream directly from the most heavily capitalized players in the entire market.
✅ Treasury Yield Reinforcement → Traders must park massive amounts of USDC inside the settlement contracts to use as margin. Lighter captures the risk-free treasury yield on these dormant stablecoin deposits through a direct revenue-share agreement with Circle. This allows the protocol to generate passive income simply by safely holding user collateral.
✅ Algorithmic Scalability Levers → By isolating the matching engine off-chain and only posting highly compressed zero-knowledge proofs to the base layer, Lighter scales infinitely. It can process billions of dollars in daily volume without bloating the underlying Ethereum network or suffering from unexpected gas fee spikes.
✅ Adoption Loop → The zero-fee structure attracts massive waves of retail traders. This deep pool of active traders naturally attracts institutional market makers who want to capture that volume. The market makers deposit massive collateral, which generates high treasury yield for the protocol. The protocol uses this revenue to improve infrastructure and deepen backstop liquidity, transforming the platform from a specialized trading tool into essential financial infrastructure.
▨ Token Utility & Flywheel
Description of the token The LIT token serves as the primary economic and governance anchor for the Lighter ecosystem. It features a strictly capped total supply of one billion units, ensuring that long-term participants do not suffer from continuous inflationary dilution.
Token Use Cases:

Payments: The protocol generates roughly $26 million in annualized revenue from premium institutional fees, liquidation penalties, and stablecoin yield. Every single dollar of this revenue is routed into systemic on-chain buybacks of the LIT token.
Rewards: Liquidity providers must hold LIT exposure to deposit capital into the Lighter Liquidity Pool. By participating in this backstop mechanism, they earn a share of the fees generated by the platform.
Staking: Institutional market makers are required to stake significant amounts of LIT to unlock the premium tier structures and gain access to prioritized execution bandwidth.
Access / Governance: Holding the token grants users voting power over the protocol parameters. This allows the community to shape future asset listings, adjust fee structures, and fine-tune the risk engine configurations.
The Flywheel:

The Lighter flywheel operates on a highly engineered mechanism of structured supply absorption. The zero-fee retail model creates an absolute explosion of trading volume. This organic volume inevitably attracts professional high-frequency trading firms. These institutional players are forced to purchase and stake massive amounts of LIT to access the premium execution lanes they desperately need to compete effectively on the platform.
{web3_wallet_create}(10x232ce3bd40fcd6f80f3d55a522d03f25df784ee2)
As the trading volume scales higher, the platform generates immense revenue from liquidation penalties and stablecoin treasury yields. Lighter takes 100 percent of this generated revenue and programmatically buys LIT off the open market. This constant, automated buy pressure, combined with the institutional staking requirements, rapidly drains the available circulating supply of the token.

A tighter token supply naturally increases the value of the rewards paid out to the liquidity providers. This encourages them to deposit even more capital into the system to capture the upside. This resulting deep liquidity creates the tightest spreads in the decentralized market, which brings in the next massive wave of retail traders to spin the entire economic wheel faster and cement the protocol as the dominant venue for digital asset derivatives.

vos.title: Market After the Fed 5 Things Crypto Traders Should Watch Next‼️‼️‼️
vos.subTitle:
The Federal Reserve has finally made its move. On September 16 the Fed raised interest rates by 25 basis points, taking its target range to 3.75%–4.00%. It was the first rate increase in more than three years.

Normally, higher interest rates create pressure on risk assets because cash and government bonds become more attractive while borrowing becomes more expensive. But crypto did something interesting: instead of falling apart after the decision, Bitcoin remained around $76,000 and parts of the altcoin market moved higher.

That tells us the rate hike itself is no longer the only story. What happens next could matter much more.

Bitcoin’s Strength Around $76K

The first thing to watch is Bitcoin itself.

Bitcoin traded around $76,000 on September 17 despite the Fed hike and earlier weakness surrounding U.S. crypto legislation. That resilience matters because traders had plenty of reasons to reduce risk.

The key question now is whether Bitcoin can turn this stability into another expansion higher or whether the post-Fed bounce fades.

Rather than focusing on every small candle, traders should watch whether BTC continues forming higher support and whether buyers remain active after the initial Fed reaction.

If Bitcoin stays stable, confidence could gradually return to the broader crypto market. If BTC begins losing important support areas, altcoins could feel the pressure much faster.

The Next Fed Move Matters More

One rate hike doesn't tell the whole story.

The Fed's latest projections indicate that most policymakers expect at least one additional increase before the end of 2026. That means the market has already started thinking about the next meeting rather than yesterday's decision.

This is important for crypto because markets trade expectations.

If inflation remains stubborn and the Fed continues signaling tighter policy, crypto could face another period of volatility. On the other hand, softer inflation or signs that further tightening is becoming less necessary could change expectations quickly.

So from here, CPI, employment numbers and other major U.S. economic releases become even more important.

Watch the Dollar and Treasury Yields

Crypto traders often spend all day looking at crypto charts, but right now the traditional markets deserve just as much attention.

The Fed decision initially pushed the U.S. dollar higher and lifted short-term Treasury yields. On September 17, the dollar gave back some of that move as yields and oil prices eased.

These markets can provide useful context for Bitcoin.

A strong dollar and rising yields can make conditions more difficult for risk assets. Falling yields and a softer dollar can reduce some of that pressure.

That doesn't mean Bitcoin will automatically move opposite the dollar every day. The relationship changes over time. But during a macro-heavy period like this one, ignoring bonds and currencies means ignoring an important part of the market.

Altcoin Rotation Could Become the Bigger Story

Bitcoin isn't the only interesting chart after the Fed.

Some altcoins have already shown stronger moves than BTC. Zcash was the standout on September 17, jumping roughly 23% while Bitcoin gained less than 1%. Solana, BNB and several other large cryptocurrencies also moved higher.

That doesn't confirm a broad altseason.

But it does show that capital isn't moving evenly across the market.

This is where traders should watch relative strength. If Bitcoin remains stable while more large and mid-cap altcoins begin outperforming, market attention could gradually shift away from BTC.

The important signal would not be one coin suddenly pumping. It would be strength spreading across multiple parts of the altcoin market.

Liquidity and Leverage Still Matter

The Fed event also showed how quickly leveraged positions can get caught when volatility increases.

Crypto can initially move one way after major news and then reverse once traders digest the details. That's why the first reaction after an FOMC announcement isn't always the most important one.

Instead of chasing a sudden green or red candle, watching liquidity, volume and whether a breakout actually holds can provide more useful information about market conviction.

This becomes especially important when the market is uncertain about future interest rates.

What Comes Next?

The Fed decision is finished, but the macro story isn't.

Bitcoin's ability to stay around $76,000 despite tighter monetary policy has given bulls something to watch. At the same time, another potential Fed hike, inflation risks and movements in Treasury yields mean the market still has important tests ahead.

For crypto traders, the next major move may come from the interaction between all of these factors rather than one headline.

Watch Bitcoin's structure. Watch the dollar and yields. Watch whether strength spreads into altcoins. And most importantly, watch how the market behaves after the news rather than reacting only to the news itself.

The Fed has made its move.

Now the market has to show us its next one.

vos.title: JPMorgan Says Bitcoin (BTC) Can Outpace Gold With IBIT Shorts Near 2026 Highs
vos.subTitle:
• JPMorgan says Bitcoin ETFs recovered only about half of 2026 outflows.
• Gold ETF inflows fully compensated for all 2026 outflows.
• IBIT short interest remains near its highest 2026 level.
Bitcoin ETF Hedging Asymmetry in Focus
JPMorgan analysts believe Bitcoin (BTC) could win meaningful ground against gold if investors begin dismantling the unusually heavy defensive positions built around cryptocurrency funds. According to the research from the team led by Nikolaos Panigirtzoglou, institutional exposure to both assets remains substantial, but Bitcoin investors are hedging far more aggressively against downside risk. The argument rests on a positioning asymmetry our flow reading suggests could become stored fuel: short interest in BlackRock's iShares Bitcoin ETF trust (IBIT) has stayed close to its highest level of 2026, while shorts in the SPDR Gold Shares ETF (GLD) sit below their historical average. A short position, for context, is a trade betting an asset's price falls. The options market echoes the split — IBIT's put-to-call open interest ratio runs higher than GLD's, a measure of how strongly demand for downside protection outweighs bullish calls, and a signal that traders are paying up to hedge a Bitcoin slide. Flows tell the first half of the story. After the Federal Reserve's July meeting, both gold and Bitcoin funds saw renewed inflows as investors rotated back into the debasement trade, the hard-asset bet that fiat erosion rewards scarce stores of value — a thesis gaining ground as China's shrinking Treasury holdings intensify the conversation. Yet gold fund inflows have already compensated for all of the outflows recorded earlier in 2026, while Bitcoin funds have recovered only roughly half of theirs. On the scoreboard alone, gold looks stronger. JPMorgan's deeper point is that the gap is defensive, not structural: the bank's X post outlining the analysis frames the hedging layer itself as capacity, since a sentiment-driven unwind of shorts and puts would mechanically add demand to Bitcoin without requiring any new capital to enter the asset class outright.
JPMorgan's Shifting 2026 Stance
The note also marks the latest step in JPMorgan's swing from constructive to cautious on digital assets across 2026. In February, Panigirtzoglou's team said it remained positive on crypto for the year, estimating the Bitcoin production cost at roughly $77,000 — down from about $90,000 at the start of the year — while reiterating a long-term, volatility-adjusted valuation of $266,000 built on a comparison with gold. Both figures still frame the current setup: the production cost model, which tracks the energy and capital outlays underpinning Bitcoin mining economics, gave the bank a floor reference for market prices, and the $266,000 number remains its long-horizon anchor. The tone hardened as the year progressed. In June, JPMorgan observed that Bitcoin had spent five consecutive months below its estimated production cost — historically a stress condition for miner margins and a source of selling pressure, since miners operating under the halving-driven issuance schedule cannot sustain losses indefinitely. Through the summer, the bank repeatedly warned that the legislative window for passing the Clarity Act, the pending US framework intended to settle how digital assets are classified, was narrowing. That regulatory uncertainty now stacks on top of a complicated institutional positioning picture: hedges elevated, ETF flows only half-recovered, and the patient accumulation behavior long associated with HODL-style institutional demand running against a shrinking policy clock. JPMorgan nonetheless holds that if investor confidence builds and protection demand fades, Bitcoin finds additional support relative to gold.
Hedge Unwind as Stored Upside
COINOTAG's read is that the hedging asymmetry functions as latent upside rather than a bearish signal. The most load-bearing record here is the bank's own ledger — gold funds have fully recovered their 2026 outflows while Bitcoin funds sit at roughly half, and IBIT shorts remain near their 2026 peaks. An unwind requires no fresh conviction, only less fear. With the Clarity Act timeline the main brake, positioning — not sentiment — is the swing variable for Bitcoin, consistent with the institutional arc in our Bitcoin digital credit market analysis.

• MoonPay's network spans more than 35 million accounts and 1,700-plus partners.
• MoonPay plans to use WTGXX in stablecoin reserve management starting in 2026.
35 Million Accounts, One Tokenized Treasury Fund
WisdomTree and MoonPay announced a strategic partnership on September 17 that opens the asset manager's tokenized Treasury fund to MoonPay's network of more than 35 million accounts. The deal centers on the WisdomTree Treasury Money Market Digital Fund (WTGXX), a blockchain-native money market mutual fund that seeks to maintain a $1 share price. Under the arrangement, WisdomTree is building an access point using MoonPay's technology, adding a second on-ramp for eligible US investors beyond its own brokerage channel. WisdomTree manages roughly $176.7 billion in assets, and MoonPay brings distribution reach across more than 1,700 partner integrations. WTGXX was already the firm's flagship tokenized money product before the deal, and the new access point does not replace WisdomTree's direct channel — it sits alongside it. WisdomTree founder and CEO Jonathan Steinberg framed the tie-up around shifting payment behavior, saying the way money moves is changing and that stablecoins are reshaping how value is held and transferred, so investing has to keep pace. The companies said in their own announcement that they expect the collaboration to broaden over time, potentially covering additional tokenized funds and markets outside the United States. Neither firm disclosed which products would come next or on what timeline, so that expansion remains unconfirmed.
The reserve side of the deal is the structurally more interesting half. MoonPay plans to fold WTGXX into its own stablecoin reserve management stack, with that integration slated for 2026. MoonPay launched its enterprise stablecoin business in November 2025 and issues dollar-denominated stablecoins across several blockchains — a multi-network footprint of the kind cross-chain bridges exist to connect — with reserves held in US dollars and other high-quality liquid assets in segregated accounts. Putting a regulated tokenized money market fund inside that reserve stack would back payment infrastructure with a yield-bearing, registered vehicle. In the joint announcement the companies shared on X, MoonPay CEO Caroline Pham, who previously served as acting chair of the CFTC, called the partnership an example of financial innovation delivering a better investor experience within America's regulated markets. One caveat deserves weight: WisdomTree explicitly states it cannot guarantee the $1 share target, and WTGXX is not a bank account and carries no FDIC insurance. For stablecoin holders, reserve composition is the difference between a durable peg and a fragile one under stress. That makes the mechanics, not the marketing, the thing to monitor.
Tokenized Treasury Market Shrinks While WTGXX Gains
Aggregate data show the partnership lands in a contracting but consolidating market. RWA.xyz figures put the tokenized US Treasury fund market at roughly $15.4 billion as of Thursday, down about 4.9% over the trailing 30 days. Within that, WTGXX held around $1.23 billion, ranking fifth among tokenized Treasury funds, while BlackRock's BUIDL led the field at approximately $2.6 billion. Flow direction is the standout: WTGXX recorded $466 million in net inflows over the past 30 days — net flows being tokens minted minus tokens burned, effectively a circulating supply change measured on-chain — and Ondo's USDY was the only other fund in positive territory, at $66 million. Fund-level metrics reinforce the trend. WTGXX had 887 holders as of Thursday, counted across wallet addresses on its issuance networks, with an estimated seven-day annualized yield near 3.61%. The token exists on Arbitrum, Solana and Ethereum, though the bulk of value sits on Ethereum, which remains the fund's primary settlement layer even as issuance spreads across chains. For a market that shrank overall, one fund absorbing nearly half a billion in new capital is a concentration signal, not a rounding error.
Reserve Backing Goes On-Chain
COINOTAG's reading: the three threads — distribution, reserves, and flows — point to tokenized Treasuries and stablecoin infrastructure converging into one stack, a DeFi 2.0 pattern where regulated yield-bearing funds back payment instruments. The companies' official announcement confirms the core terms: WTGXX access through MoonPay's technology, more than 35 million accounts, and a stated plan to use the fund in reserve management from 2026, with possible expansion into additional tokenized funds globally. What is not disclosed matters equally: no timeline for non-US markets, no named stablecoins, and no reserve allocation percentage. The cleanest test is WTGXX's holder base — 887 addresses as of Thursday — and whether it climbs once the integration goes live.

vos.title: How the $2HATS Smart Contract Collects and Distributes Funds 🎩🎩
vos.subTitle:
How the $2HATS Smart Contract Collects and Distributes Funds
Contract Address (BSC): 0x40fc200e43725771923e4bd8bec3115af8c6ffff
View on BscScan: https://bscscan.com/address/0x40fc200e43725771923e4bd8bec3115af8c6ffff
One of the most common questions in the $2HATS community is: "How does the tax actually work, and when does that money show up in the treasury or mining pool?" This article breaks down the mechanics step by step, using the published wallet registry from the official project site.
1. How the Tax Is Collected
Every time $2HATS is bought or sold on-chain, the smart contract automatically applies a small transaction tax:
Buy tax: 1%
Sell tax: 2%
This isn't sent anywhere at the moment of the trade. Instead, like most BEP-20 tax tokens on BNB Chain, the contract collects the taxed tokens and holds them in its own contract balance first. You can verify this at any time by checking the token balance held by the contract address itself on BscScan.
2. The 90/5/5 Revenue Split
Once collected, the tax allocation is divided as follows:
90% — Project treasury and $BTCB mining pool funding
5% — Reserved allocation (operations/marketing)
5% — Reserved allocation (liquidity support)
This split is what funds the $BTCB mining pool, the $JACK faucet, and the referral program over time — it's the economic engine behind the ecosystem, not just a static tax.
3. From Contract Balance to Wallet: The Swap-and-Send Step
Collected tax tokens sitting in the contract don't do anything useful as raw $2HATS — they need to be converted. The contract uses a swap-and-send mechanism:
The contract accumulates taxed $2HATS tokens from buys and sells.
Once the accumulated balance reaches the equivalent of 0.01 BNB, the swap threshold triggers.
At that point, the accumulated tokens are automatically swapped via PancakeSwap into BNB, then routed toward $BTCB accumulation.
The converted funds are sent to the project's published revenue and treasury wallets according to the 90/5/5 split.
Because the threshold is a fixed BNB value rather than a fixed token count, how often it triggers depends on trading activity and the current token price. Busier trading days mean the threshold fills faster and distributions happen more frequently. Quiet periods mean it takes longer to accumulate enough taxed tokens to hit 0.01 BNB, so the swap-and-send event fires less often.
4. The Published Wallet Registry
Per the project's official "Wallets in one lane" registry, here is where funds actually land after conversion:
Role
Address
Revenue receiver
0x54d320d19bf011df984fee3910f4c0dc9e6186a3

The revenue receiver is the first stop after the swap-and-send trigger fires — this is the wallet that catches the converted tax. From there, funds move toward the treasury/controller wallet, which is the lane that funds both ongoing treasury $BTCB accumulation and the mining pool. The project has not published a separate, standalone wallet exclusively for the mining pool distinct from the treasury/controller address — the treasury/controller appears to serve both roles.
5. Important: Distribution Timing
This is the part the community should understand clearly: funds collected by the contract do not move instantly, and reaching the receiver wallet is not the final step either.
Tax collection happens in real time with every buy/sell.
Conversion and movement to the revenue receiver only happen once the 0.01 BNB threshold is reached — not continuously, and not on every single trade.
From the revenue receiver, funds are then routed onward to the treasury/controller wallet for $BTCB accumulation and mining pool funding — this is a second step, and it doesn't necessarily happen on the same schedule as the initial swap-and-send.
Depending on trading volume, gas conditions, and price movement, there can be a noticeable delay between when tax is first collected and when it's fully reflected in the treasury or mining pool balance.
In short: if you check the treasury wallet right after a trade and don't see funds move yet, that's expected. Tokens may be sitting in the contract awaiting the 0.01 BNB threshold, or sitting in the revenue receiver awaiting the next transfer to treasury. Nothing has gone missing — it's a multi-step routing process by design. The project encourages the community to track balances over days, not minutes, for an accurate picture of treasury and mining pool growth.

vos.title: CRO Issuer Crypto.com's Nadex Wins SEC Registration for Single-Stock Futures
vos.subTitle:
• The SEC acknowledged Nadex's Form 1-N on Sept. 16, filed Sept. 14, effective at submission.
• Nadex is owned by Crypto.com, the issuer of the CRO token.
• Marszalek said single-stock futures are authorized; perps need SEC and CFTC approval.
SEC Clears Nadex for Stock Futures
The Securities and Exchange Commission on Sept. 16 acknowledged the Form 1-N registration filed by North American Derivatives Exchange (Nadex), the futures exchange owned by Crypto.com — the company behind the CRO token that powers the Cronos chain. Under Section 6(g) of the Securities Exchange Act, a CFTC-regulated board of trade may register “solely for the purposes of trading security futures products” by submitting a written notice, and that registration “becomes effective contemporaneously with the submission.” In practical terms, Nadex became a registered national securities exchange for stock futures the moment it filed on Sept. 14 — no commission vote, no waiting period. The SEC release confirms only that staff in its Division of Trading and Markets reviewed the notice for completeness and proper form; it names no product. Security futures occupy a hybrid regulatory position: the underlying asset is a security, but the contract itself is a futures instrument, so both the SEC and the Commodity Futures Trading Commission hold authority. Nadex already operates as a CFTC-designated contract market and clearing organization, and it routes trading through OG.com, the trader-focused venue Crypto.com is spinning off as an independent company.
Single-Stock Perps Need Both Regulators
Kris Marszalek, Crypto.com’s co-founder and chief executive, confirmed the milestone in a post on X on Wednesday evening, writing that the filing covered the company’s futures exchange through OG.com and that “we are now authorized to bring single-stock futures to the market.” The registration clears the first regulatory hurdle, but the product Marszalek ultimately wants — perpetual futures on individual US stocks, a format native to crypto derivatives that keeps positions open indefinitely and pins price to spot through a funding-rate mechanism rather than a fixed expiry, as our guide to futures trading explains — requires sign-off from both the SEC and the CFTC. On that front he named no launch date, no underlying stocks and no leverage limits, and the SEC’s acknowledgment is silent on perpetuals. The exchange’s credentials run long: the CFTC registry shows Nadex was designated a contract market in 2004 as HedgeStreet, was acquired by Foris DAX Markets in March 2022 and now does business under the Crypto.com name, while a September 2025 amendment authorized margined futures cleared on an intermediated basis by registered futures commission merchants.
Coinbase and Robinhood Race In
Crypto.com is not alone in this push. Coinbase Derivatives filed its own Form 1-N on Sept. 1, which the SEC acknowledged a week later on Sept. 8 — a step toward listing perpetual futures on individual stocks that likewise requires CFTC approval. The broader land-grab for traditional-market exposure on crypto venues has been building all year: Coinbase launched stock perpetuals for non-US users in March and rolled out regulated crypto futures alongside 24/5 cash-equity trading in the US in February, while Kraken is working with the London Stock Exchange toward overnight sessions for tokenized UK stocks in 2027. Robinhood has moved furthest, from tokenized shares with voting rights to integrated equity and crypto trading inside a single app. The connections to OG.com specifically are already live: Robinhood began routing football event contracts to the venue this month and agreed to take equity stakes in both Crypto.com and OG.com once the spin-off completes, deepening the tie-up that lifted CRO to a weekly high earlier this cycle.
CRO Ecosystem’s TradFi Bridge Widens
The arc here is consolidation: crypto exchanges are rebuilding the full brokerage stack around their tokens, and the filing COINOTAG reviewed makes the mechanics explicit — registration took effect upon submission and names no product, meaning the single-stock futures language is Crypto.com’s own description of what it intends to list. For Cronos holders, the parent company’s push into US-regulated equities and derivatives extends the utility case for the layer 1 network’s native asset at a moment when the platform is backed by fresh institutional capital. The faster OG.com converts registration into listed products, the more tradable the CRO ecosystem’s traditional-finance bridge becomes.

vos.title: US Energy Department Launches $215 Million Quantum Contest With Bitcoin (BTC) Security in Focus
vos.subTitle:
• US Energy Department launched the Quantum Genesis Q Competition with up to $215 million in funding.
• The contest requires fault-tolerant quantum computers with at least 100 logical qubits.
• The wider federal program targets quantum system deployment by 2028.
Quantum Genesis Q Competition Opens With $215 Million
The United States has put federal money behind the machine that could one day test Bitcoin's cryptography. On Thursday, the Department of Energy opened the Quantum Genesis Q Competition, a contest backed by up to $215 million in funding and aimed at pushing quantum computing from laboratory promise toward working hardware. In a post announcing the initiative, the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy described the Q Competition under Quantum Genesis as the next step in advancing quantum computing toward mainstream utility, with the Energy Department leading the technical effort.
The contest asks private companies to demonstrate what organizers call “scientifically relevant,” fault-tolerant quantum computers. The technical floor is precise: a minimum of 100 logical qubits, plus sustained runs numbering in the hundreds of millions of reliable operations. A logical qubit, unlike the noisy physical qubits inside today's hardware, is an error-corrected unit of quantum information — and fault tolerance is the technique that keeps long calculations from collapsing under noise. Today's machines degrade quickly, which limits their usefulness for serious science, so clearing this threshold would show for the first time that large, error-corrected quantum computations can run at meaningful scale rather than in fragmented experiments.
The wider program carries the more consequential marker: deployment by 2028. That is a fixed calendar date, something the quantum debate around Bitcoin has never had. Until now, discussion of quantum risk has been open-ended — a threat without a schedule. A funded federal competition with a deployment target changes the shape of that conversation, converting an abstract worry into an engineering roadmap whose milestones outsiders can track. Neither the White House nor the Energy Department has published a per-project funding breakdown, and the submission deadline was not disclosed in the announcement.
The Qubit Gap and 6.04 Million Exposed BTC
Why this matters for Bitcoin comes down to one algorithm. Bitcoin proves ownership through elliptic-curve cryptography: the network verifies a signature against a public key, and only the matching private key can produce a valid one. A sufficiently powerful quantum machine running Shor's algorithm could invert that relationship, deriving a private key from a public key that has already been broadcast to the network.
Researchers at Google estimated earlier this year that breaking the 256-bit elliptic-curve system Bitcoin uses would take roughly 1,200 to 1,450 logical qubits, depending on the machine's design. The Energy Department's floor of 100 sits well below that line. But hitting it would establish that error-corrected architectures scale — the prerequisite step every downstream estimate of the danger depends on.
Exposure, meanwhile, is not hypothetical. On-chain analysis published in May counted about 6.04 million BTC, equal to 30.2% of issued supply, sitting in outputs whose public keys were already visible on-chain. Those coins — including the earliest Satoshi-era holdings — would present the clearest targets once quantum key-breaking becomes practical, which is why even circles committed to Bitcoin maximalism treat the subject as more than background noise.
Developers are not starting from zero. Draft proposals BIP 360 and BIP 361 outline routes to reduce public-key exposure and eventually move away from today's vulnerable signature schemes. A migration of that scope would touch wallets, exchanges, custodians and ordinary users simultaneously; judging by the pace of past protocol changes such as Segregated Witness, it could take years to complete. The effort now joins a widening set of technology-policy questions around the network, alongside the AI nuclear red lines researchers urged as Bitcoin held near $76K.
2028 Deadline Reshapes the Migration Debate
The competition does not put Bitcoin's proof-of-work design or its mining layer in danger — hashing, not signatures, secures block production. Key exposure is the vulnerability. What changed this week is that Washington attached a budget and a date to a threat that previously had neither. Our reading of the announcement: the math still favors Bitcoin, with the qubit gap measured in the thousands, but a funded federal roadmap carrying a 2028 marker makes the dormant BIP 360 debate progressively harder to leave parked.

vos.title: Ondo (ONDO) Heirs Petition Hawaii Court to Curb 77-Year-Old Kathleen Allman's Estate Control
vos.subTitle:
• Nathan Allman died suddenly in May at 32 without a will; probate court named his parents inheritors.
• Lani Clinton and David Chen petitioned a Hawaii court for a limited conservatorship over Kathleen Allman's share.
• Kathleen Allman, 77, sued acting CEO Ian De Bode over an $11 million compensation package.
Hawaii Conservatorship Petition
The succession fight at Ondo Finance escalated this week as founder Nathan Allman's half-sister, Duke University medicine professor Dr. Lani Clinton, and early Ondo backer David Chen petitioned a Hawaii court for a limited conservatorship over Kathleen Allman's share of the estate. The 77-year-old mother of the late founder inherited the position alongside her husband Lawrence after Nathan Allman died suddenly in May at age 32, leaving no will, with a probate court naming the couple inheritors of an estate that, per the petition, holds a controlling equity interest in the tokenized-assets firm and a very large stash of ONDO, its governance token, spanning both unlocked supply and tokens scheduled to release over the next three years. The petitioners allege Kathleen Allman suffers from a long-standing alcohol use disorder alongside progressively impaired judgment and social cognition that leaves her unable to manage assets of this magnitude, and they have asked the judge to review her medical records and evaluate her for dementia, pointing to a pattern they say matches the behavioral variant of frontotemporal dementia. The filing also catalogs alleged lavish spending: Nathan Allman bought his parents an $18.5 million beachfront home in Honolulu in June 2025, while court documents describe a roughly $4 million Zeelander yacht purchase attempt in Florida, private aircraft travel and lodging at about $4,000 per night. Nine days after her son's death, the filings state, Kathleen texted Chen that her top concern was cash flow, citing a $200,000 pool invoice and a boat she wanted to buy. Clinton says she has been estranged from her mother since 2022. Through her lawyers, Kathleen Allman rejected the petition as a baseless personal attack, filed by an associate of acting CEO Ian De Bode after his efforts to take control of the company were declared invalid by the Delaware Court of Chancery.
The $11 Million Compensation Fight
The management struggle crystallized in the days right after the founder's death. Ian De Bode took over as acting CEO, while Kathleen Allman installed herself and her daughter Tahnee Towill on Ondo's board, named herself chair and interim CEO, and moved to strip De Bode of all company positions. A Sept. 3 court order, however, keeps De Bode in place as acting CEO and a director. She subsequently sued him, accusing him of a brazen usurpation of corporate control and alleging he began plotting a compensation package worth roughly $11 million within a week of Allman's death. Her complaint seeks a ruling that De Bode and Chen were never validly appointed to the board, that the disputed awards are void, and damages for alleged breaches of fiduciary duty. The package described in the complaint included a $900,000 annual salary and bonus, a $1 million signing bonus, and 26 million restricted token units valued at more than $9 million; awards covering 846,000 shares would have lifted De Bode's stake from 0.33% to roughly 8%, a 24-fold increase, with vesting set to begin May 25 — the day after Allman died. The estate's complaint quipped that even the writers of Game of Thrones could not have scripted the power grab better. A Delaware court has already invalidated De Bode's attempts to wrest control, and Kathleen Allman said in a statement that she has prioritized good governance from day one and will keep supporting Ondo's long-term success while upholding her son's vision. The company itself has declined to comment.
Three Years of Unlocks at Stake
Read against the docket itself — the Sept. 3 order, the Hawaii petition and the Delaware Chancery posture — the dispute is at bottom a fight over custody of supply. Whoever prevails controls a controlling equity stake plus ONDO tokens that will keep vesting for three more years, a pool of potential exit liquidity at scale, though this is a court-supervised succession battle, not a rug pull in any market sense. It is also unfolding while the commercial engine runs independently: the protocol recently led tokenized stocks to a record 2.96 million holders and continues to press regulators to onshore stock perpetuals. With the Ondo ecosystem's governance overhang now inseparable from the token market, ONDO's spot price swung 8.1% over the past 24 hours as the new filings landed.

vos.title: Polymarket Hires Zora Co-Founder for Polygon DeFi Rebuild, Its Third Hire in Eight Days
vos.subTitle:
• Polymarket hired Zora co-founder Jacob Horne to rebuild its onchain trading product.
• Shayne Coplan announced the hire Thursday and promised a town hall on product fixes.
• Horne left Zora after more than six years running the social-token app.
Jacob Horne Returns to Product Work
Prediction-market operator Polymarket has hired Jacob Horne, the co-founder who spent more than six years running the social-token application Zora, to rebuild its onchain trading product. Chief executive Shayne Coplan announced the appointment on Thursday, eight days after Horne stepped away from Zora. Prediction markets let users trade contracts tied to real-world outcomes — elections, rate decisions, sports — with prices reflecting the crowd's collective odds, a mechanism distinct from crypto options, which settle on asset prices instead, and Polymarket became the best-known crypto venue for exactly that kind of trading.
The company runs a split-venue model. Traders outside the United States use a market that settles on the Polygon blockchain — the side of the business that functions as a genuine DeFi trading app — while American users trade on a separate venue licensed by the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) to offer futures-style contracts. Horne's mandate targets the first of those two rails. In his own announcement post, Coplan wrote that the new product lead will be “working closely with me on product, in particular making Polymarket DeFi great again.” Horne is a product founder rather than a finance hire: at Zora he built the tooling that let creators mint social posts into tradeable assets, experience that maps closely onto prediction markets as consumer crypto products with a settlement layer underneath.
There is an admission behind the hire. Coplan acknowledged that the onchain product had weakened as the company scaled and that longtime users had come to believe it was abandoned. He promised a town hall to lay out the fix — an unusually public concession for a platform that at its peak became the default venue for election markets. The role also drops Horne directly against Kalshi, the exchange that now powers Coinbase's own prediction markets across the United States, giving the rebuild a competitive urgency well beyond product polish.
A Coinbase Castoff and Kalshi's Grip
Horne's arrival carries an awkward backdrop, because his former company built the product Coinbase just abandoned. Zora let people turn social posts into tokens others could trade on Base, the Ethereum layer-2 network Coinbase created — a speculative mechanic closer to an ICO-era mindset than to regulated markets. Coinbase championed the creator-coin thesis for more than a year before its own leadership conceded the bet had failed. Brian Armstrong said the coins did not work; Zora was among several Base experiments the exchange dropped this year, and Coinbase even restored the Coinbase Wallet name to its products this month.
Coinbase did not abandon prediction markets themselves — it routed its US product through Kalshi instead. Kalshi operates as a CFTC-regulated exchange, which is why Coinbase chose it as the rails for American users. That choice shows up starkly in the volume split: Kalshi handled $13.1 billion of the $15.8 billion traded across the two platforms in the week ending September 13, leaving Polymarket with 17% — roughly one in six prediction-market dollars. That is the market context Horne inherits.
The hire is also the third senior appointment in eight days. Warren Jenson — previously chief financial officer at Amazon, where Coplan says he worked directly with Jeff Bezos, and later at Electronic Arts and Delta — became Polymarket's first CFO on September 10, per the company's own announcement. Collin McKinney Hill, a former DoorDash general manager, joined as vice president of operations on September 15. Product, finance and operations are being rebuilt at once — a pace that signals an organizational reset ahead of the promised town hall. vos.title: "$62,000,000 in Shiba Inu Futures Positions Remain Open as Traders Face Fresh Liquidations"
vos.subTitle:
#Shiba Inu traders are holding more than $62 million in open futures positions, even as overall derivatives activity remains relatively subdued.
According to CoinGlass data, Shiba Inu’s open interest stood at $62.25 million, while its 24-hour futures volume reached $54.42 million.
As a result, open interest has moved above daily futures turnover, indicating that traders are maintaining a significant amount of leveraged exposure rather than actively rotating those positions through the market. 

Futures Trading Dominates SHIB Spot Activity
Meanwhile, the derivatives market currently accounts for much of Shiba Inu’s trading activity.
Notably, Shiba Inu recorded approximately $54.25 million in 24-hour futures volume, compared with roughly $19.99 million in spot volume. Therefore, futures trading was about 2.7 times higher than spot activity.
Despite the derivatives-heavy market, SHIB has posted a modest gain. The token climbed 3.99% over the past 24 hours to $0.000005040 at press time. Shiba Inu’s market valuation also increased by the same percentage to approximately $2.96 billion, with SHIB currently ranked as the 29th-biggest crypto in the world.  

Long Traders Account for Most SHIB Liquidations
However, the recent recovery has not prevented leveraged traders, particularly those betting on higher prices, from taking losses.
According to data from CoinGlass, a total of 73 SHIB traders recorded $182,650 in liquidations over the past 24 hours. Long positions accounted for most of these losses, with about $162,740 in long positions liquidated, compared with $19,910 in short positions.
This imbalance comes as SHIB remains below its weekly high of $0.0000054. Although the token has recovered nearly 4% over the past day, its earlier decline this week has continued to pressure bullish leveraged positions. 

249 Billion SHIB Leaves Exchanges Amid Rising Burn Activity
At the same time, exchange flows point to increased SHIB withdrawals, potentially reducing the amount of tokens immediately available for selling on centralized exchanges.
Data from CryptoQuant shows that 249.40 billion SHIB left exchanges, although the total exchange reserve remains above the 87 trillion SHIB mark. The current reserve stands at 87.06 trillion SHIB.
Additionally, SHIB’s burn activity has accelerated sharply. The daily burn rate has jumped 716% over the past 24 hours after the community burned 27.36 million SHIB during that period. Meanwhile, total burns over the past week have reached 118 million SHIB, adding another notable development to the token’s recent market activity.

vos.title: BitMEX Delists XBTUSD, Ending 12-Year Run of the First Bitcoin (BTC) Perpetual
vos.subTitle:
• BitMEX settled and delisted the XBTUSD perpetual contract, with the platform shutting down on September 23.
• XBTUSD launched on May 13, 2016 as the world's first perpetual swap with no expiry date.
• BitMEX raised XBTUSD leverage to 250x in April 2024 via the Leverage Booster feature.
One Contract, Twelve Years, No Expiry
BitMEX has settled and delisted XBTUSD, the contract that gave traders their first leveraged Bitcoin (BTC) market with no expiry date, and the platform itself goes offline on September 23. XBTUSD launched on May 13, 2016 and ran for more than a decade — an unusually long life for a derivatives product that broke every convention of traditional futures. Conventional futures expire on fixed dates, forcing traders to roll positions and splitting liquidity across a calendar of contracts. XBTUSD removed that friction entirely: one continuous market, one order book, liquidity concentrated instead of fragmented. That single design choice is why the delisting reads as a structural event rather than routine housekeeping. BitMEX also engineered the funding mechanism that still defines perpetuals, keeping the contract price pinned near spot: when too many traders crowd onto one side of the trade, they pay the other side, dragging the mark back toward the spot rate. Leverage followed. At launch, traders could control $100 of Bitcoin exposure for every $1 they posted; the ceiling later climbed to 250x in April 2024 for accounts that activated the Leverage Booster feature. For retail traders in 2016, the format collapsed the complexity of rolling futures into something closer to spot trading with margin. In its farewell thread, the exchange credits co-founders Arthur Hayes, Ben Delo and Samuel Reed, who kept returning to one question — why should a market that trades around the clock be forced onto expiring futures? — an idea BitMEX says began as scribbles on a napkin in a Hong Kong bar. The exchange’s official announcement positions XBTUSD as the world’s first perpetual swap, and market history bears that out: every venue that followed copied the template rather than replacing it.
Perpetuals Now Exceed 75% of Crypto Volume
XBTUSD’s influence outgrew BitMEX years before the delisting. Binance, Bybit, OKX and Hyperliquid each run their own perpetual implementations, and BitMEX’s own figures put perpetual contracts at more than 75% of total crypto trading volume — laid out in its closing data post — a share that now defines the broader Bitcoin market. The format is also marching beyond crypto-native venues. Kalshi filed with US regulators in August to offer stock index perpetual futures, and Kraken’s parent company intends to bring Hyperliquid perpetuals to US traders through a regulated venue, pushing the expiry-free design into conventional markets accustomed to wrappers such as the spot ETF complex. BitMEX closed with a stark record: “12 years. 0 customer funds lost. Every bull and bear cycle crypto has ever had.” That claim covers funds lost to security breaches, not losses traders incurred trading — a distinction worth flagging. Celsius sued five BitMEX entities on September 12 over 6,360 Bitcoin lost to forced liquidations in the March 2020 crash, a whale-scale sum that sits squarely outside the exchange’s hack-free definition. Traders weighing where perpetual volume consolidates next can also follow our running coverage of the best crypto exchanges, which tracks how top venues structure leverage and funding today.
A Structure That Outlives Its Creator
COINOTAG’s read: the delisting is administrative; the market-structure shift is not. The primary record — BitMEX’s own posts, from the founding-napkin thread to the shutdown notice and the 75%-of-volume breakdown — documents a product that became the default venue for leveraged BTC exposure and then escaped its inventor entirely. The open question is whether Kalshi’s US filing and Kraken’s parent’s regulated rollout replicate the funding mechanic or dilute it. XBTUSD is gone; the market it invented is still expanding.
